channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: PHP 8.6 arrives with partial function application and safer defaults
item.description: PHP 8.6 adds partial function application, the Time\Duration and Io\Poll APIs, a clamp function and more secure session defaults. The migration guide deserves attention before a server upgrade, but the release offers practical improvements for modernizing a long-lived PHP codebase.

item.title: Betty Boop ruling explains why trademark cannot recreate expired copyright
item.description: The Ninth Circuit’s Fleischer Studios v. A.V.E.L.A. opinion is a useful case study for public-domain character publishing. It rejected an attempt to use trademark law as a substitute for expired copyright in Betty Boop imagery, while leaving room for claims tied to genuinely source-identifying uses.
item.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

item.title: Jacksonville library opens searchable access to three newspaper archives
item.description: Jacksonville Public Library now offers cardholders online access to the Florida Times-Union back to 1883, the Beaches Leader back to 1963 and the Jacksonville Journal from 1901 through 1988. Full-page scans preserve photographs, comics, advertisements and neighborhood details useful for local-history research.

item.title: A careful guide to deciding when old serial issues are public domain
item.description: The Online Books Page lays out a decision tree for newspapers, magazines and similar serials, including registration, notice, renewal and independently copyrighted contributions. Its examples explain why a public-domain issue can still contain protected comics, and why publication date and issue date are not always the same.

item.title: SPSFC 6 opens entries for self-published science-fiction novels
item.description: The sixth Self-Published Science Fiction Competition is taking first-time entries through November 29 unless it fills earlier. Eligible books must be self-published science-fiction novels of at least 40,000 words, published by December 7; each author gets one entry, and prior non-semifinalists enter during a later resubmission window.

item.title: A practical tour of WordPress RSS feeds, GUIDs and migration traps
item.description: This guide goes beyond finding WordPress’s `/feed/` URL to explain alternate feeds, caching, discovery tags and what happens after a domain move. Its most useful warning is to preserve each post’s GUID: changing those identifiers can make feed readers treat an archive as newly published and redeliver every item.

item.title: AWS updates its practical guide to choosing Lightsail, Beanstalk or EC2
item.description: AWS’s September 29 decision guide compares the three hosting paths by control, pricing, deployment and growth. It describes Lightsail as the predictable, unified choice for straightforward websites, Beanstalk as managed application deployment and EC2 as the option for maximum infrastructure flexibility.

item.title: PHP’s official migration guide maps the breaking jump from 7.4 to 8.0
item.description: The PHP manual’s incompatibility list is the best first checklist before moving an old site to PHP 8. It covers fatal inheritance-signature errors, stricter string and number handling, removed functions, resource-to-object changes and altered return values—the changes most likely to surface in long-lived WordPress-era code.

item.title: NASCAR’s official guide puts every 2026 television and streaming outlet in one place
item.description: NASCAR’s updated viewing guide links the season’s television and streaming homes: FOX, FS1 and FS2; Prime Video; TNT Sports; NBC and USA; The CW; plus app and international options. The page is refreshed weekly, making it a useful bookmark when races and supporting series move between networks.

item.title: A practical map to Florida HOA covenants and amendments
item.description: This guide explains why a Florida HOA’s declaration and amendments are found in county official records, while articles of incorporation are filed with Sunbiz and board-made rules often must come from the association. It includes links for all 67 counties and useful search terms when a clerk’s document types are unclear.

item.title: The advanced numbers behind Colorado’s disappointing season
item.description: This pre-Houston snapshot uses ESPN’s Football Power Index and related efficiency measures to explain Colorado’s 2026 struggles after a 3-6 start. It separates the Buffaloes’ reputation from their opponent-adjusted performance and offers a useful baseline for comparing them with North Texas.

item.title: A birthday-ready guide to Weird Tales writer Mary Elizabeth Counselman
item.description: Born November 19, 1911, Mary Elizabeth Counselman wrote 30 horror and fantasy stories for Weird Tales, including “The Three Marked Pennies,” composed when she was 15. This detailed biography traces her Alabama settings, newspaper work, unusual women-centered pulp fiction and later Arkham House collection.

item.title: How to read a publisher royalty statement and its reserves
item.description: Cornell University Press explains the columns authors encounter on royalty statements, including sales, returns, prior balances and reserves against future returns. Particularly useful is its distinction between the reserve withheld this period and reserves from earlier periods that have now been released.

item.title: Why the 1984 Lensman anime remains trapped in rights limbo
item.description: This history traces the licensing problems behind the vanished Lensman film and television series. It reports that Harmony Gold never finalized its U.S. license, Streamline withdrew its releases after the Smith estate threatened legal action, and any revival would require negotiations whose cost may exceed the small vintage-anime market.

item.title: Copyright Office finishes digitizing 26,000 historical record books
item.description: The U.S. Copyright Office has completed digitization of more than 26,000 record books containing registrations, assignments, notices and other documents from 1870 through 1977. The images are available in a Library of Congress preview collection, with searchable metadata planned for the Copyright Public Records System.
